problemStatement.title: Problem Statement
problemStatement.description: Cross-border investment in emerging markets is hindered by three systemic problems:

remoteOversightGap.title: Remote Oversight Gap
remoteOversightGap.description: Investors funding projects in countries where they are not physically present have no reliable way to verify that work is being done, that funds are being used correctly, or that milestones are being met.

trustDeficitInTransactions.title: Trust Deficit in Transactions
trustDeficitInTransactions.description: High-value transactions between parties who do not know each other, or who operate across jurisdictions, carry significant risk. Buyers cannot verify goods before payment. Sellers cannot guarantee payment after delivery. There is no neutral party to hold funds, verify delivery, or arbitrate disputes.

informalFinancialCoordination.title: Informal Financial Coordination
informalFinancialCoordination.description: Group contribution models (such as Susu, chama, and tontine systems) remain largely informal. Funds are managed manually, contribution tracking is opaque, payout schedules are unstructured, and there is no mechanism for dispute resolution or accountability when contributors default.

marketContext.title: Market Context
marketContext.description: The African diaspora alone remits over $95 billion annually, with a significant portion directed toward real estate, construction, agriculture, and small business ventures. A large share of these funds are managed through informal channels with limited oversight.

faqsSection.subtitle: Find answers to common questions about Nnarks.

items.question: What is Nnarks?
items.answer: Nnarks is a trust infrastructure platform that helps diaspora investors and partners manage remote projects securely using milestone-based escrow and verified execution.

items.question: How does the escrow work?
items.answer: Funds are held securely in a multi-currency escrow. They are only released to the local partner or contractor when specific, pre-defined milestones are met and verified.

items.question: Who verifies the milestones?
items.answer: Milestones can be verified by uploading GPS-tagged, time-stamped evidence (photos, videos, documents), or by assigning a verified Nnarks on-ground supervisor.

items.question: How do group contributions work?
items.answer: Group contributions allow you to manage Susu, Chama, or Tontine models efficiently with automated contribution tracking and payout scheduling.

items.question: Are my funds secure?
items.answer: Yes, all funds are securely locked in escrow accounts governed by strict release conditions. You have full visibility over where and when your money moves.
